findings.title: Unit Conversion Verification Needed for CO Storage
findings.location: Section 1.4 (US EPA Implementation), unit conversion comment
findings.issue: The design's EPA conversion function assumes CO input in µg/m³, but CO is actually stored in mg/m³ according to normalize.py lines 74-82.
findings.fix: Clarify the conversion function should accept mg/m³ for CO: `return concentration / 1145  # mg/m³ to ppm (CO stored in mg/m³)`

findings.title: Location.country_code Migration Not Specified
findings.issue: The design adds country_code field but doesn't specify how to handle existing Location records without a country_code.
findings.fix: Add migration guidance: existing locations can have NULL country_code and get populated on next search/refresh. Optionally backfill Indian locations with 'IN'.

findings.title: European AQI Gauge Scale Mapping Unclear
findings.issue: Ambiguous whether the API returns the band number (1-6) or the mapped value (25-150) for European AQI.
findings.fix: Clarify in Section 2.2: aqi.value contains the mapped index (25, 50, 75, 100, 125, or 150), not the raw band number.

findings.title: Pollutant Averaging for European AQI Not Detailed
findings.issue: Doesn't specify whether 'daily mean' uses rolling 24-hour window or calendar day.
findings.fix: Add clarification: European AQI uses rolling 24-hour averages for PM2.5/PM10 (same as CPCB), and latest 1-hour values for NO2/O3/SO2. Minimum 18 hours coverage for 24h averages.

findings.title: Error Handling for NO2/SO2 EPA Conversions Not Specified
findings.issue: EPA uses 1-hour NO2/SO2 but database may have 24-hour from CPCB. Handling for mismatched periods not specified.
findings.fix: Add to Section 1.4: Prefer 1-hour measurements if available, otherwise exclude NO2/SO2 from EPA calculation rather than using mismatched periods.

summary: Design is ready for implementation. All HIGH and MEDIUM findings from previous review have been addressed. Breakpoints are verified/sourced from official EPA and EEA documentation. Architecture preserves separation of concerns. Backward compatibility maintained. Five NIT findings are minor clarifications that won't block implementation.
